source_fact: The Renewable Expansion Act establishes that total electricity consumption should be covered nationally and on balance by 100% renewable energy from 2030.
expected_entities: Austria; Renewable Expansion Act; Renewable Electricity 2030
expected_relationship: Austria HAS_TARGET 100% nationally balanced renewable electricity by 2030
pilot1_audit_notes: Austria and the Renewable Expansion Act were extracted, but the 100% renewable-electricity target for 2030 was not represented as a dedicated structured target entity. The Act was typed as EVENT or ORGANIZATION. Relationship assessment: Relationships involving the Renewable Expansion Act and Austria exist, but none preserves the specific 100% renewable-electricity target for 2030.
pilot2_entity_evidence: ERNEUERBAREN-AUSBAU-GESETZ (EAG) and the TARGET entity 100% BILANZIELL ERNEUERBARER STROMVERBRAUCH BIS 2030.
pilot2_relationship_evidence: EAG SETS_TARGET 100% nationally balanced renewable electricity consumption by 2030; Austria also HAS_TARGET.
pilot2_audit_notes: Policy, target value, geographic scope and 2030 deadline are explicitly represented.

source_fact: The Renewable Expansion Act provides for at least 11 TWh of additional photovoltaic generation by 2030 compared with 2020.
expected_entities: Renewable Expansion Act; Photovoltaics; 11 TWh; 2030
expected_relationship: Renewable Expansion Act HAS_TARGET 11 TWh of additional PV generation by 2030
pilot1_audit_notes: The Renewable Expansion Act and Photovoltaics were extracted, but the 11 TWh target and its 2030 date were not represented as dedicated target/value entities. Several aliases and inconsistent types exist. Relationship assessment: The Renewable Expansion Act is connected to Photovoltaics and renewable-energy expansion, but the specific 11 TWh target for 2030 is absent.
pilot2_entity_evidence: EAG, PHOTOVOLTAIK and PV-AUSBAU VON MINDESTENS 11 TWH BIS 2030 are extracted.
pilot2_relationship_evidence: EAG SETS_TARGET PV expansion of at least 11 TWh by 2030, with an explicit connection to photovoltaics.
pilot2_audit_notes: The legal instrument, technology, numerical quantity, deadline and comparison context are represented.

source_fact: RED III raises the EU renewable-energy share target to 42.5%, with 45% to be aimed for, by 2030.
expected_entities: RED III; European Union; 42.5%; 45%; 2030
expected_relationship: RED III HAS_TARGET EU renewable-energy share by 2030
pilot1_audit_notes: RED III and the European Union were extracted, but the 42.5% target, 45% ambition and 2030 deadline were not represented as structured target entities. RED III also appears under different raw types. Relationship assessment: RED III is connected to the European Union and Austria, but the 42.5% target, 45% ambition and 2030 deadline are absent from the relationship structure.
pilot2_entity_evidence: EU-ERNEUERBAREN-RICHTLINIE (RED III), the European Union and the renewable-energy-share target are extracted.
pilot2_relationship_evidence: RED III SETS_TARGET the renewable-energy share, including the 42.5%, 45% ambition and 2030 context.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 represents this numerical EU policy target as a policy-to-target relationship rather than a generic event.

source_fact: Austria introduced a zero-percent VAT measure for eligible PV systems with a capacity of up to 35 kWp.
expected_entities: VAT Exemption; PV System; 35 kWp
expected_relationship: VAT Exemption SUPPORTS PV System up to 35 kWp
pilot1_audit_notes: The VAT exemption and PV installations were extracted, but the 35 kWp eligibility threshold was not represented as a dedicated structured entity or attribute. The support scheme was typed as EVENT. Relationship assessment: A relationship description mentions the VAT exemption for PV systems up to 35 kWp, but its endpoints connect the exemption to VAT rather than directly representing the support relationship between the exemption and eligible PV systems.
pilot2_entity_evidence: UMSATZSTEUERBEFREIUNG FÜR PV-ANLAGEN BIS 35 KWP is extracted as SUPPORT_SCHEME, together with PV-ANLAGE.
pilot2_relationship_evidence: The zero-percent VAT support scheme and eligible PV installation threshold are represented, but the displayed relationship candidates do not clearly preserve the complete support-scheme-to-35-kWp relationship in one edge.
pilot2_audit_notes: The important entities and threshold are captured. The exact support relationship should still be verified before treating the fact as fully structured.

source_fact: The proposed Electricity Industry Act includes simplified grid connection for small systems and greater transparency concerning grid capacities and development plans.
expected_entities: Electricity Industry Act; Grid Connection; Grid Capacity
expected_relationship: Electricity Industry Act SUPPORTS simplified and transparent grid connection
pilot1_audit_notes: The Electricity Industry Act, E-Control and grid-connection action plans were extracted. However, simplified grid connection and grid capacity transparency were not represented as clear controlled entities. Multiple aliases of the Act were produced. Relationship assessment: Relationships involving the Electricity Industry Act, Austria and EU legislation exist, but simplified grid connection and grid-capacity transparency are not represented completely.
pilot2_entity_evidence: ELEKTRIZITÄTSWIRTSCHAFTSGESETZ (ELWG), NETZANSCHLUSS, NETZANSCHLUSSVERFAHREN, VERTEILERNETZ and related infrastructure concepts are extracted.
pilot2_relationship_evidence: Multiple relationships connect the ELWG to distribution-grid regulation, grid access, digital infrastructure and PV systems. The complete compound claim concerning simplified access for small systems, transparency, capacity data and development plans is distributed across several edges.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 captures the policy and its principal components, but not the complete compound fact as one precise relationship.

source_fact: The planned Renewable Expansion Acceleration Act is intended to accelerate procedures for PV installations and required infrastructure.
expected_entities: Renewable Expansion Acceleration Act; PV Installation; Infrastructure
expected_relationship: Renewable Expansion Acceleration Act SUPPORTS accelerated permitting
pilot1_audit_notes: The Renewable Expansion Acceleration Act, PV installations and infrastructure concepts were extracted. The essential concepts are present, although the Act is incorrectly typed as EVENT and duplicate E-ABG/EABG forms exist. Relationship assessment: The acceleration act is related to federal legislation and expedited renewable infrastructure deployment, but the specific permitting relationship for PV installations is incomplete.
pilot2_entity_evidence: ERNEUERBAREN-AUSBAU-BESCHLEUNIGUNGSGESETZ appears as POLICY, including EABG and E-ABG variants.
pilot2_relationship_evidence: The act SUPPORTS photovoltaic installations, simplified procedures, procedural exemptions and PV uses in infrastructure.
pilot2_audit_notes: The planned act and its intended acceleration mechanisms are explicitly represented, although alias resolution is still needed.

source_fact: Building law, spatial planning and nature conservation are primarily responsibilities of the Austrian federal states.
expected_entities: Federal States; Building Law; Spatial Planning; Nature Conservation
expected_relationship: Federal States IMPLEMENT policy in building, spatial-planning and conservation areas
pilot1_audit_notes: The federal states were extracted, but building law, spatial planning and nature-conservation responsibilities were not consistently represented as separate controlled concepts. Bundesländer was typed as GEO. Relationship assessment: Separate relationships connect nature conservation and spatial planning to the federal states. However, the complete responsibility covering building law, spatial planning and nature conservation is fragmented and building law is not clearly represented.
pilot2_entity_evidence: BUNDESLÄNDER and NATURSCHUTZ are extracted, together with state-level targets and land-related concepts. Building law and spatial planning are not clearly represented as corresponding controlled entities in the displayed evidence.
pilot2_relationship_evidence: Federal states are linked to land availability, permitting simplification and target setting, while nature conservation constrains PV. The complete assignment of building law, spatial planning and nature conservation to federal-state responsibility is not represented in one complete relationship structure.
pilot2_audit_notes: The central actor and part of its responsibilities are captured, but the full responsibility statement is fragmented.

source_fact: The Federal-State Dialogue on Renewable Energy coordinates federal and state targets, land availability, processes and support strategies.
expected_entities: Federal-State Dialogue on Renewable Energy; Federal Government; Federal States
expected_relationship: Federal-State Dialogue COORDINATES renewable-energy implementation
pilot1_audit_notes: The Federal-State Dialogue, Federal Government and Federal States were extracted. The core actors are present, although the dialogue was typed as ORGANIZATION and broad entities such as BUND remain overgeneralized. Relationship assessment: The Federal-State Dialogue is connected to the federal government and federal states, and policy harmonization is mentioned. Detailed coordination of targets, land, processes and support strategies is not fully preserved.
pilot2_entity_evidence: BUND-LÄNDER-DIALOG ERNEUERBARE ENERGIE is extracted, together with BUND and BUNDESLÄNDER.
pilot2_relationship_evidence: The dialogue is explicitly associated with the federal government and federal states and linked to renewable targets. Coordination of land availability, processes and support strategies is not fully expressed in the displayed edges.
pilot2_audit_notes: The coordinating mechanism and participating government levels are captured, but the complete scope of coordination is incomplete.

source_fact: The 2022 amendment to the Condominium Act made the construction of PV systems on terraced houses and individual buildings easier.
expected_entities: Condominium Act Amendment 2022; PV Systems; Buildings
expected_relationship: Condominium Act Amendment SUPPORTS residential PV installation
pilot1_audit_notes: The Condominium Act amendment, PV systems and relevant building concepts were extracted. The main source concepts are present, but the law was typed as EVENT rather than POLICY or LAW. Relationship assessment: Relationships explicitly connect the Condominium Act amendment with easier PV installation and terraced houses. The essential meaning of the source fact is preserved.
pilot2_entity_evidence: WOHNUNGSEIGENTUMSGESETZ-NOVELLE 2022 and its spelling variant are extracted as POLICY entities.
pilot2_relationship_evidence: The amendment SUPPORTS photovoltaic installations and is linked explicitly to terraced houses and individual buildings.
pilot2_audit_notes: The policy amendment, relevant building types and support for PV construction are explicitly represented. Duplicate policy names require later entity resolution.

source_fact: The Austrian Photovoltaic Strategy is intended to be a living document that is adjusted when conditions change.
expected_entities: Austrian Photovoltaic Strategy; Changing Conditions
expected_relationship: Austrian Photovoltaic Strategy EVOLVES_WITH changing conditions
pilot1_audit_notes: The Austrian Photovoltaic Strategy was extracted, including shortened duplicate names. However, its status as a living document that should change with future developments was not represented as a separate process or property. Relationship assessment: The Austrian Photovoltaic Strategy has several relationships, but none represents its status as a living document that should be updated when conditions change.
pilot2_entity_evidence: The Austrian Photovoltaic Strategy is extracted as POLICY, but the living-document or adaptive-policy characteristic is not clearly represented as a separate entity.
pilot2_relationship_evidence: The displayed strategy relationships cover targets and action fields, but no relationship explicitly states that the strategy is revised or evolves when conditions change.
pilot2_audit_notes: The strategy itself is strongly represented, but its adaptive or living-document property was not converted into a structured relationship.

source_fact: Austria reached 6.3 TWh of PV generation in 2023.
expected_entities: Austria; PV Generation; 6.3 TWh; 2023
expected_relationship: Austria MEASURED_BY 6.3 TWh PV generation in 2023
pilot1_audit_notes: Photovoltaics and Austria were extracted, but 6.3 TWh of PV generation in 2023 was not represented as a dedicated structured market-metric entity. Relationship assessment: No relationship represents Austria reaching 6.3 TWh of PV generation in 2023.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted the 6.3 TWh PV-generation metric, Austria, Photovoltaics and the year 2023, with a relationship representing the measured PV-generation result.

source_fact: Approximately 2.5 GW of new photovoltaic capacity was installed in Austria in 2023.
expected_entities: Austria; Annual PV Expansion; 2.5 GW; 2023
expected_relationship: Annual PV Expansion MEASURED_BY 2.5 GW in 2023
pilot1_audit_notes: PV expansion and Austria were represented generally, but the 2.5 GW addition in 2023 was not represented as a structured metric with value, unit and year. Relationship assessment: No relationship represents approximately 2.5 GW of new PV capacity in 2023.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted the annual PV-capacity addition of approximately 2.5 GW in Austria in 2023 and represented it through an explicit measured relationship.

source_fact: One GW of new photovoltaic capacity was installed in Austria in 2022.
expected_entities: Austria; Annual PV Expansion; 1 GW; 2022
expected_relationship: Annual PV Expansion MEASURED_BY 1 GW in 2022
pilot1_audit_notes: Photovoltaic expansion was represented generally, but the 1 GW addition in 2022 was not represented as a dedicated market-metric entity. Relationship assessment: No relationship represents 1 GW of new PV capacity in 2022.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted the annual PV-capacity addition of 1 GW in Austria in 2022 and represented the numerical result through an explicit measured relationship.

source_fact: The Integrated Austrian Network Infrastructure Plan identifies 41 TWh of photovoltaic generation potential by 2040.
expected_entities: Network Infrastructure Plan; Photovoltaics; 41 TWh; 2040
expected_relationship: Network Infrastructure Plan HAS_TARGET 41 TWh PV by 2040
pilot1_audit_notes: The Network Infrastructure Plan and Photovoltaics were extracted, but the 41 TWh by 2040 target was not represented as a dedicated target containing value, unit and deadline. Relationship assessment: The Network Infrastructure Plan and PV concepts have relationships, but no relationship preserves the 41 TWh target for 2040.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted the Integrated Austrian Network Infrastructure Plan, Photovoltaics and the 41 TWh by 2040 target. However, the meaning is distributed across relationships rather than represented as one direct NIP-to-target relationship.

source_fact: At least approximately 15 TWh of the 2040 PV potential is considered achievable on existing and new buildings.
expected_entities: Buildings; PV Potential; 15 TWh; 2040
expected_relationship: Buildings CONTRIBUTE_TO 15 TWh PV potential by 2040
pilot1_audit_notes: Buildings and PV-related concepts were extracted, but the 15 TWh building potential was not represented as a structured metric or target. Relationship assessment: No relationship represents approximately 15 TWh of PV potential on existing and new buildings.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted the building-based PV potential of approximately 15 TWh by 2040 and connected it to the broader 41 TWh photovoltaic potential.

source_fact: An average expansion rate of approximately 2 GW per year is needed to reach the 2040 PV potential.
expected_entities: Annual PV Expansion; 2 GW per year; 2040
expected_relationship: PV Expansion HAS_TARGET approximately 2 GW per year
pilot1_audit_notes: PV expansion and the 2040 context appear in generated descriptions, but the required average rate of approximately 2 GW per year was not represented as a dedicated metric. Relationship assessment: No relationship represents the required average PV expansion rate of approximately 2 GW per year.
pilot2_audit_notes: The annual expansion target of approximately 2 GW per year and the 2040 PV potential are represented as entities, but no relationship directly connects the annual rate to achieving the 2040 potential.

source_fact: The Transition 2040 scenario requires 21 TWh of photovoltaic electricity generation in 2030.
expected_entities: Transition 2040; Photovoltaics; 21 TWh; 2030
expected_relationship: Transition 2040 HAS_TARGET 21 TWh PV generation in 2030
pilot1_audit_notes: Transition 2040 and Photovoltaics were represented, but the 21 TWh requirement for 2030 was not represented as a structured target. Relationship assessment: No relationship represents the Transition 2040 requirement of 21 TWh of PV generation in 2030.
pilot2_audit_notes: The Transition 2040 scenario and the 21 TWh PV-generation target for 2030 were extracted. However, the target is connected to Austria rather than directly to the Transition 2040 scenario, so the relationship provenance is only partially represented.

source_fact: The 21 TWh requirement for 2030 represents an increase of 19 TWh compared with 2020.
expected_entities: PV Expansion; 19 TWh; 2020; 2030
expected_relationship: PV Expansion MEASURED_BY 19 TWh increase from 2020 to 2030
pilot1_audit_notes: PV expansion and the relevant years occur in generated output, but the 19 TWh increase between 2020 and 2030 was not represented as a structured market metric. Relationship assessment: No relationship represents the 19 TWh increase required between 2020 and 2030.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted the 21 TWh requirement for 2030 and the required 19 TWh increase compared with 2020. A direct explicit-fact relationship connects the 21 TWh requirement with the 19 TWh increase.

source_fact: Approximately EUR 600 million was provided for PV expansion in 2023 through the Renewable Expansion Act and Climate and Energy Fund.
expected_entities: Renewable Expansion Act; Climate and Energy Fund; EUR 600 million; 2023
expected_relationship: Renewable Expansion Act and Climate and Energy Fund SUPPORT PV expansion
pilot1_audit_notes: The Renewable Expansion Act and Climate and Energy Fund were extracted, but the approximately EUR 600 million provided in 2023 was not represented as a dedicated funding-value entity. Relationship assessment: Relationships connect the Renewable Expansion Act and Climate and Energy Fund to PV support, but none preserves the approximately EUR 600 million funding value for 2023.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted the EUR 600 million PV funding metric for Austria in 2023. Explicit FUNDS relationships connect both the Climate and Energy Fund and the Renewable Expansion Act to this funding metric.

source_fact: At the end of 2023, PV supplied almost 10% of Austria's final electricity consumption and approximately 2% of total energy demand.
expected_entities: Photovoltaics; Final Electricity Consumption; Energy Demand; 10%; 2%; 2023
expected_relationship: Photovoltaics MEASURED_BY electricity and energy shares in 2023
pilot1_audit_notes: Photovoltaics and Austrian energy concepts were extracted, but the approximately 10% electricity share and 2% total-energy share in 2023 were not represented as structured indicators. Relationship assessment: No relationship represents PV supplying almost 10% of final electricity consumption and approximately 2% of total energy demand at the end of 2023.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted separate MARKET_METRIC entities for the approximately 10% share of final electricity consumption and approximately 2% share of total energy demand in Austria in 2023. Explicit MEASURED_BY relationships connect Austria and photovoltaics to these metrics.

source_fact: Digitalization of the distribution grid is important for integrating renewable and decentralized electricity.
expected_entities: Distribution Grid; Digitalization; Renewable Electricity
expected_relationship: Digitalization SUPPORTS renewable-electricity grid integration
pilot1_audit_notes: The distribution grid was extracted, but digitalization specifically as a technical enabler of decentralized renewable integration was not represented as a complete controlled entity structure. Relationship assessment: The distribution grid is connected to the broader electricity grid, and digitalization appears in other relationships. However, the specific relationship that distribution-grid digitalization supports decentralized renewable integration is missing.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted DIGITALISIERUNG, STROMNETZ, VERTEILNETZ and decentralized-energy concepts. It also created a SUPPORTS relationship from DIGITALISIERUNG to STROMNETZ. However, the complete source claim linking digitalization of the distribution grid specifically to the integration of renewable and decentralized electricity is distributed across multiple graph records rather than represented as one complete relationship.

source_fact: Photovoltaic generation peaks can no longer always be completely absorbed by the public electricity grid.
expected_entities: PV Generation Peaks; Public Electricity Grid
expected_relationship: Public Electricity Grid CONSTRAINS PV generation peaks
pilot1_audit_notes: The electricity grid and Photovoltaics were extracted, but PV generation peaks and the grid's inability to absorb them completely were not represented as dedicated entities. Relationship assessment: The grid is connected to smart energy management and storage solutions for handling PV generation. However, the explicit fact that PV peaks can no longer always be completely absorbed by the public grid is not preserved.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted photovoltaic generation peaks as a CONSTRAINT and the electricity grid as INFRASTRUCTURE. An explicit CONSTRAINS relationship connects PHOTOVOLTAIK-ERZEUGUNGSSPITZEN to STROMNETZ.

source_fact: Smart local energy management and storage can manage generation and consumption peaks and increase self-consumption.
expected_entities: Energy Management; Energy Storage; Self-Consumption
expected_relationship: Energy Management and Storage SUPPORT peak management and self-consumption
pilot1_audit_notes: Smart local energy management and storage-related concepts were extracted, but self-consumption and generation/consumption peak management were not fully represented as separate concepts. Relationship assessment: Smart local energy management is connected to the grid and customer installations for balancing and PV optimization. Storage and self-consumption are not completely preserved in one supported relationship.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted smart energy management, storage technologies, peak prevention and self-consumption concepts. It also extracted relationships connecting energy-management systems and storage to the prevention of feed-in and load peaks. However, the complete source claim—including both peak management and increased self-consumption—is distributed across several records rather than represented by one complete relationship.

source_fact: PV should operate synergistically with electric mobility, heat pumps, hydrogen and other generation and storage technologies.
expected_entities: Photovoltaics; E-Mobility; Heat Pumps; Hydrogen; Storage
expected_relationship: Photovoltaics INTEGRATES_WITH other energy technologies
pilot1_audit_notes: Photovoltaics, e-mobility, heat pumps, hydrogen and storage-related technologies were extracted. The essential technical concepts are present, although several received unsuitable generic GraphRAG types. Relationship assessment: Photovoltaics has separate relationships with some energy technologies, including hydrogen-related systems. The complete synergistic integration with e-mobility, heat pumps, hydrogen and storage is fragmented rather than represented as one fact.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted Photovoltaics, e-mobility, and hydrogen as TECHNOLOGY entities. However, heat pumps and sector coupling were not identified in the displayed candidates, and no relationship represents the stated synergistic operation among these technologies.

source_fact: East-west-oriented and vertical PV installations can provide higher PV yields during shoulder and winter periods.
expected_entities: East-West PV; Vertical PV; Winter Yield
expected_relationship: PV Orientation CONTRIBUTES_TO broader generation periods
pilot1_audit_notes: General PV concepts were extracted, but neither east-west-oriented PV nor vertical PV was represented as a dedicated entity. The specific technical approach for shoulder and winter generation was therefore missed at the entity level. Relationship assessment: No relationship represents east-west-oriented or vertical PV installations as methods for improving generation during shoulder and winter periods.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted a general TECHNOLOGY entity for PV installations in different orientations. However, east-west orientation, vertical orientation, and their higher yields during shoulder and winter periods were not represented precisely. No relationship captures the seasonal yield benefit.

source_fact: Agri-PV enables combined agricultural and photovoltaic use and can increase land-use efficiency.
expected_entities: Agri-PV; Agriculture; Land-Use Efficiency
expected_relationship: Agri-PV CONTRIBUTES_TO agricultural dual use
pilot1_audit_notes: Agri-PV installations were extracted, but agricultural dual use and land-use efficiency were not represented as complete controlled concepts. Agri-PV was also typed as ORGANIZATION. Relationship assessment: Relationships explicitly represent Agri-PV as combined agricultural and photovoltaic land use and mention improved land-use efficiency. The essential source meaning is preserved.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted Agri-PV, agriculture, farmers, dual land use, and several relevant relationships. It clearly represents the combination of agricultural and photovoltaic use. However, the specific claim that Agri-PV increases land-use efficiency is not represented as a precise direct relationship.

source_fact: Open-space PV installations should be designed as biodiversity installations in accordance with defined ecological criteria.
expected_entities: Open-Space PV; Biodiversity PV; Ecological Criteria
expected_relationship: Open-Space PV IMPLEMENTS biodiversity criteria
pilot1_audit_notes: Open-space PV and several biodiversity-PV concepts were extracted, but the requirement to follow defined ecological criteria was not represented as a separate controlled concept. Relationship assessment: Relationships connect open-space PV with biodiversity installations and ecological enhancement. However, the requirement to follow defined ecological criteria is not fully preserved.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted open-space PV installations, biodiversity PV installations, biodiversity and nature-protection concepts. It also connected FREIFLÄCHENANLAGE with BIODIVERSITÄTS-PV-ANLAGE. However, the requirement to design installations according to defined ecological criteria was not represented completely as a structured relationship.

source_fact: PV systems should be installed on federal buildings wherever technically and economically possible.
expected_entities: Federal Buildings; PV Systems; Technical Feasibility; Economic Feasibility
expected_relationship: Federal Buildings SUPPORT PV deployment when feasible
pilot1_audit_notes: Federal buildings and PV systems were extracted, but the technical and economic feasibility conditions were not represented as structured constraints. Relationship assessment: Federal buildings are identified as targets for PV deployment, but the conditions that deployment should occur only where technically and economically feasible are missing.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted general PV-system, building, technical, and economic concepts, but it did not extract federal buildings as a distinct entity. It also did not represent the complete relationship stating that PV systems should be installed on federal buildings wherever technically and economically possible.

source_fact: Energy communities should be further developed using storage, consumption flexibility, real-time monitoring and control.
expected_entities: Energy Communities; Storage; Flexibility; Real-Time Monitoring
expected_relationship: Storage and Flexibility SUPPORT development of Energy Communities
pilot1_audit_notes: Energy communities, storage and flexibility concepts were extracted, but real-time operational monitoring and the complete implementation combination were not represented as structured entities. Relationship assessment: Energy communities are connected to PV and shared storage, but the complete combination of storage, consumption flexibility, real-time monitoring and control is not represented.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted energy communities, storage, flexible consumers, flexibility incentives and related concepts. Several relevant relationships were extracted, but the complete source statement connecting energy communities with storage, consumption flexibility and real-time mechanisms was not represented as one explicit structured relationship.

source_fact: PV research should address resource efficiency, durability, repairability, reuse and recycling of PV components.
expected_entities: PV Research; Resource Efficiency; Durability; Repair; Reuse; Recycling
expected_relationship: PV Research CONTRIBUTES_TO PV circular economy
pilot1_audit_notes: PV circular economy and repair were extracted, but resource efficiency, durability, reuse and recycling were not all represented as separate controlled concepts. Relationship assessment: PV circular economy, repair and recycling appear in relationships, but resource efficiency, durability, reuse and the full research objective are not represented together.
pilot2_audit_notes: Pilot 2 extracted research and innovation, circular economy, resource efficiency, durability, repair, recycling and related PV concepts. Several supporting relationships were generated, but the complete source statement was distributed across multiple entities and relationships rather than represented as one precise relationship connecting PV research to all stated objectives.
